panel_intro: One question at a time — nothing here is submitted anywhere.

danger.text: Is the vehicle at risk of tipping, sinking further, or is anyone in immediate danger (water, unstable ground)?

own_equipment.text: Do you have your own winch or tow strap and another vehicle to help, safely?

emergency.title: Call Emergency Services Now
emergency.summary: If the vehicle could tip, sink further, or anyone is in danger from water or unstable ground, call 911 before attempting any recovery yourself.
emergency.confidence_text: Situations involving water, unstable ground, or tipping risk are always treated as urgent.
not_to_do: Don't attempt a DIY recovery in a situation that could worsen or become dangerous.
Don't stay in or near a vehicle at risk of sinking or tipping.
Don't wait to see if the situation stabilizes on its own.
before_help_checklist: Move away from the vehicle if there's any risk to you.
Call 911 and describe the exact situation and location.
Keep others away from the immediate area.

lines: My vehicle is stuck and at risk of [tipping / sinking / another hazard] at [location description].
No one is currently injured, but this is dangerous.

emergency.next_action: Stay somewhere safe until help arrives.

self_recovery.title: Safe to Reassess — Careful Self-Recovery
self_recovery.summary: With a proper strap or winch and another vehicle, a careful self-recovery from mud, snow, or sand can be reasonable — but only using rated recovery points, never a bumper or random tow hook.
self_recovery.confidence_text: This assumes both vehicles and equipment are actually rated for this — if you're unsure, treat it as a professional-winch situation instead.
not_to_do: Don't attach a strap to a bumper, tie rod, or anything not a rated recovery point.
Don't stand near a strap or chain under tension — a snapped strap can whip back with serious force.
Don't use a nylon strap that's frayed, cut, or visibly worn.
before_help_checklist: Confirm both vehicles have rated recovery points.
Keep bystanders well clear of the strap's path.
Pull slowly and steadily — don't jerk the vehicle free suddenly.
Check the strap and attachment points before and during the pull.

phone_script.intro: Keep this ready in case the recovery doesn't work.
lines: Hi, I'm stuck at [location description] and attempting a self-recovery.
Can you confirm ETA for a professional winch-out in case I need to call back?

self_recovery.next_action: If it doesn't come free within a couple of careful attempts, stop and call a professional winch-out instead of forcing it.

professional_winch.title: Do Not Drive — Call a Tow
professional_winch.summary: A ditch, embankment, or a stuck vehicle without the right equipment on hand calls for a professional winch-out — attempting it yourself risks further damage or a worse situation.
professional_winch.confidence_text: Without rated equipment and a safe setup, this isn't a reasonable DIY situation.
not_to_do: Don't attempt to rock or force the vehicle free repeatedly — it can dig you in deeper or cause damage.
Don't accept help from an underequipped bystander's vehicle for anything beyond light mud or snow.
Don't stand near any strap or cable under tension.
before_help_checklist: Note exactly how the vehicle is stuck (angle, depth, obstacle) to describe to the operator.
Confirm exactly where you want the vehicle taken if it needs more than a simple winch-out.
Keep bystanders clear of the recovery area.
Ask about total price before work begins — winch-outs often have a separate fee from a standard tow.

phone_script.intro: Read this while you're on the phone with the tow company.
lines: Hi, my vehicle is stuck in [mud / snow / a ditch] at [location description] and needs a winch-out.
Can you confirm total price for the winch-out, ETA, and whether that includes towing afterward if needed?

professional_winch.next_action: Use the Tow Cost Estimator's winching option to sanity-check the price before you agree.
